Leaving Ukraine

By: Anina Peens | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As we return from Ukraine, we reflect on the war and our experiences on the ground

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche spent two weeks on Ukrainian territory. As we return home, we discuss the latest developments as we reflect on our experiences.

Summary:
After the grim discovery of hundreds of dead bodies in Bucha, a town near the Ukranian capital Kyiv, fear in Ukraine escalates. Although Russia denied responsibility for what appears to be a mass murder, it is refocussing its military efforts to the Eastern and Southern Regions of the country. A city at great risk of attacks, is Odessa, where tighter curfew restrictions were instated on Friday. This comes after Russia's first attack on the city last Sunday. Missiles were also fired on Monday and Tuesday but the rest of the week was seemingly calm.

Further information:
a Strict cufew was instated this weekend in Odessa, Ukraine's largest and vital port city. This weekend was a memorial day of the liberation of Odessa from the Nazis' during World War Two. The curfew was instated to prevent large gatherings that could be easy targets for attacks. Russia first fired missiles on the city last week which destroyed an oil depot and storage facility that supplied Ukrainian military troops in Mykoliev about 100km from Odessa. This is after Ukraine, a few days earlier, alledgedly fired missiles to a oil facility in Russia near the border with Ukraine. This depot supplied Russian military bases in Kharkiv. Ukraine neither confirmed nor denied this attack. But these attacks make sense. If Russia gets control of Ukraine's ports like Odess, Mykoliev, Kherson and Mykoliev, it takes control of the economy. What does not make sense, is why Russia will fire missiles onto a train station, killing civilians, as we saw on Friday morning.
